Work ONLY in this repository and on the current branch. Read AGENTS.md first and obey its UX/design rules. This is Local Climate Link mobile UI polish, starting with Dashboard. Do not change Shelly/BLE/automation-core semantics, safety behavior, networking, persistence formats, or unrelated architecture. Reuse existing runtime/control APIs and components; do not invent parallel logic. Keep changes small, clean, typed, testable, and avoid god components.

Visual target: a compact calm mobile dashboard like a polished native smart-home app. The accepted reference from the user has: one-line title at top, refresh and settings as equal compact icon buttons aligned on the same row; no filler subtitle; compact segmented climate/time selector; dense readable automation cards with title/status and controls arranged horizontally where space allows; ON/OFF and Auto/Manual controls visible without inflating the card; data hierarchy is temperature first, humidity secondary, other useful values compact; minimal borders/shadows; no obvious explanatory copy; no artificial vertical padding. The reference is inspiration, but preserve all useful current information unless the user explicitly asked to remove it.

User-requested Dashboard fixes that MUST be addressed now:
1. Remove the dashboard sentence equivalent to 'Podgląd tego, co aktualnie widzi i robi każde Shelly.' Do not replace it with filler. Also remove any redundant kicker if it only consumes vertical space.
2. Fix the settings/refresh action regression: actions should be symmetrical, compact and visually aligned in the top header. The global settings icon must no longer force the title/content down via an artificial extra top row. Prefer a small reusable shell/header solution over one-off positional hacks.
3. Make each automation card meaningfully shorter while retaining useful data. Do not reduce touch targets below project tokens/accessibility rules.
4. Restore visible ON/OFF and Manual/Auto controls on climate automation cards by reusing the exact existing runtime control semantics already used elsewhere in the app. Do not implement new automation behavior. Buttons must reflect pending/disabled/error state safely.
5. When the last automation is removed, do not show a redundant empty Dashboard. Route directly to the existing 'Co chcesz zrobić?' intent screen. Ensure zero-installation startup and post-delete behavior converge on that canonical screen.
6. Keep time automation cards coherent with the same visual system, but do not break their current schedule behavior.
7. Prefer design tokens and existing shared UI primitives. No hardcoded theme colors.

Before editing, inspect AutomationDashboardScreen, TimeAutomationCard, App/App shell, AppRoutes, InstallationDetail/Time detail and existing runtime control hooks to identify the canonical control calls. Then implement the smallest coherent change. Add/update focused tests for routing zero state and restored Dashboard controls/layout where practical. Do not touch generated artifacts except screenshots produced later by the outer task. Do not commit or push; leave changes in the working tree for outer verification.
EOF
